requirement: Do not invent a required operating pressure, source condition, flow or downstream limit. Every pressure and flow is an illustrative study case (IL-nn) or an unresolved input (UI-nn).
The nitrogen source is a boundary interface that can be isolated by two block valves with a bleed between them, so isolation can be proved.
source_basis: Precedent: NASA-STD-5005D 5.2.6(b) (GN2 into ECS ducting; read, not applied)

requirement: Pressure is reduced in stages by regulators. A regulator is not overpressure protection.

Every zone downstream of a regulator is designed for the source pressure or protected by a relief device that passes the failed-open regulator flow. Set pressures, capacities and discharge are fixed from real data.
Every zone that can trap gas has a controlled depressurization path to the vent through a restrictor.
source_basis: Concept rationale: trapped gas between regulators

requirement: Pressure and temperature of each zone are monitored, local gauges allow verification and calibration, and cold gas after the regulators is detected.
Downstream flow is controlled and measured. The flow-control valve drop is carried as an unresolved row until the downstream limits are known.
A check valve is used only where backflow is credible, and is never relied on for isolation.
source_basis: Task brief, phase 2 (check valves where justified)

requirement: Relief and bleed discharge route to a safe location, no valve is in a relief path, and the back-pressure is checked against relief-device limits.
The oxygen-deficiency hazard is screened and its controls (ventilation, oxygen monitoring) are shown.
Test and maintenance interfaces give leak check, gauge calibration and proof of isolation without opening the process line.
An independent trip is separate from the flow loop and does not replace a relief device. Trip settings and failure positions are not assumed.
The pressure budget separates controlled drops from losses, gives low, nominal and high cases, flags unresolved rows, and shows sensitivity to line diameter and component losses.
Joule-Thomson cooling of each stage is accounted for with verified property data.
The pressure-system classification and governing design code are identified as items for review. No rating or component is selected.
Operating states and valve positions are defined for pressurization, delivery, hold, depressurization and shutdown. Failure positions are not assumed.
implemented_in: HIGH_PRESSURE_SYSTEM.md; HV-301; HV-302; HV-303; HV-304; HV-305; HV-306; XV-301

requirement: Any flexible hose connection at the delivery interface has restrained ends.
Liquid nitrogen only: no liquid oxygen, liquid hydrogen, propellant, combustion or hazardous operating trial.
The source vessel is a boundary interface with its own relief and vent. No capacity or pressure is assumed.
An insulated (vacuum-jacketed) transfer line concept is given with a documented heat-leak model.
Do not assume a cryogenic line can be isolated safely when liquid may be trapped. Every liquid-capable section has a relief path to a safe location and a vent path stays open.
Thermal contraction and support movement are accommodated by a movement device and sliding supports. The inner line is not restrained axially.
Heat leak and boil-off are estimated with a documented model. The source vessel evaporation rate and terminations are not calculated until data exist.
Relief and venting philosophy: cold vapour or liquid discharge goes to a safe location. Vent sizes, relief settings and the location are not given.
Temperature, pressure, vacuum and level are measured.
Materials are compatible with the cryogenic service: low-temperature toughness, seals, and the liquid-air condensation hazard are addressed.
Cooldown, normal transfer, shutdown and warm-up states (with purge, stop and emergency) and their valve positions are defined.
implemented_in: CRYOGENIC_SYSTEM.md; HV-401; XV-401; HV-402; HV-403; HV-405

requirement: A check valve on the purge connection prevents liquid backflow into the purge line.
A phase separator takes the two-phase flow of the cooldown.
The oxygen-deficiency hazard is screened and its controls (ventilation, oxygen monitoring) are shown.
An independent trip is separate from control and does not replace relief devices.
The vacuum jacket is protected against an inner-line leak and its vacuum is monitored.
Two-phase flow and hydraulic-transient considerations are identified. No number is produced without data.
Personnel exposure to cold surfaces, liquid and cold vapour is controlled by insulation, guarding and procedures.
Verified data, equations, illustrative assumptions and calculated results are kept separate.
The calculations are screening only. No claim is made of vessel or piping integrity, relief-device sizing or code compliance.
Every diagram is marked CONCEPTUAL — NOT APPROVED FOR CONSTRUCTION. and shows flow direction, system boundaries, operating states and vent or discharge boundaries.
Tags are consistent across diagrams, schedules, line lists and documents, and no unsupported size or rating is given.
Numerical outputs regenerate deterministically, and the numbers in the documents and diagrams equal the calculated values.
No restricted standard is stored or reproduced, and no compliance is claimed from a title or summary page alone.
No existing repository file is modified except a minimal root README link.
Missing inputs are documented and not fabricated. Calculations refuse unresolved inputs.
The heated-duct rig remains a low-pressure air system. No CFD, Mechanical, LS-DYNA, SQL or air-rig file is modified or rerun.
No private paths, secrets or unintended third-party content are in the new files.
The checks fail meaningfully when a source value or an important output is corrupted (mutation tests in the validation report).
